cases.answer: Natural keyboard focus follows DOM order and focusable native controls. Positive tabindex jumps ahead into a separate numbered order. Visual order stays where it was. Now keyboard users encounter fields in a different sequence. Keep the source order logical rather than numbering your way around it.
cases.notes: Consequence is expressed in adjacent sentences without because. Fully explains why manual positive ordering is discouraged.

cases.answer: A stale element points to a node from the old dome after a rerender or navigation replaced it. Wait for the current page condition and locate the element again using its locator, then retry the action within a bound. Reusing the old reference keeps targeting the detached node.
cases.notes: Dome is an obvious DOM transcription substitution. Correct stale-reference mechanism and recovery, no penalty for spelling.

cases.answer: A DOM replacement can detach the node held by the element reference. Locate the current element again rather than reusing that reference. Also, a sufficiently long implicit wait repairs any detached reference permanently because time reattaches the same object.
cases.notes: Meaningful correct cause and recovery mixed with explicitly false wait/reattachment claim. Retain true knowledge; mixed/false reasoning must not be fully MET.

cases.answer: Selenium automates browsers. StaleElementReferenceException always means the remote server has permanently lost its internet connection; changes to the DOM never cause it. The sound recovery is to disable every timeout permanently and keep the same element reference.
cases.notes: Browser automation is an incidental true fact, not correct knowledge of stale-element cause or recovery. Central beliefs are clearly false. Contrast with meaningful correct cause/recovery plus a false addition in N15-08.
